name: FixedFloat
rootCause: According to on-chain data, the cryptocurrency exchange FixedFloat appears to have been exploited, resulting in the theft of approximately $26.1 million worth of Bitcoin and Ethereum. On February 18th, FixedFloat tweeted: "We confirm that there was indeed a hack and theft of funds. We are not yet ready to make public comments on this matter, as we are working to eliminate all possible vulnerabilities, improve security, and investigate. Our service will be available again soon. We will provide details on this case a little later."

descriptions.text: According to on-chain data, the cryptocurrency exchange FixedFloat appears to have been exploited, resulting in the theft of approximately $26.1 million worth of Bitcoin and Ethereum. On February 18th, FixedFloat tweeted: "We confirm that there was indeed a hack and theft of funds. We are not yet ready to make public comments on this matter, as we are working to eliminate all possible vulnerabilities, improve security, and investigate. Our service will be available again soon. We will provide details on this case a little later."

On February 16, 2024, FixedFloat’s hot wallets were compromised via a key or signing authority breach, resulting in the theft of ~$26 million from both Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets. The attacker moved BTC to CoinJoin via Samourai Wallet and sent ETH through the eXch coin-mixer, with no published technical postmortem or details on the specific compromise vector. The attacker gained signing authority over FixedFloat’s operational hot wallets, draining all BTC and ETH on hand. The FixedFloat cryptocurrency exchange was exploited for around 409 BTC (~$21.17 million) and 1,728 ETH (~$4.85 million) for a total loss of just over $26 million. FixedFloat is a decentralized cryptocurrency exchange that doesn't require user registration or Know Your Customer , making it popular for hackers looking to launder stolen funds. FixedFloat first wrote that they had "encountered some minor technical problems", then acknowledged that there had been a hack. FixedFloat is non-custodial, so no user funds were impacted, however some have reported frozen transactions and missing funds from using the service on social media.
